hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Estimate with easier numbers first: $14 \times 4.5$ is $63$. An estimate like this tells you where the decimal point must go.
Decimal points can be left out during the multiplication and put back at the end. Count how many decimal places the two factors have altogether.
Multiply $136 \times 45$ by adding $136 \times 40$ and $136 \times 5$. Each factor has one decimal place, so the product needs two.
$5440 + 680 = 6120$, and with two decimal places the product is $61.20$, which is $61.2$.

explanation: Drop the decimal points and multiply the whole numbers $136 \times 45$ in two parts.
The parts are $136 \times 40 = 5440$ and $136 \times 5 = 680$, and their sum is $6120$.
Each factor has one decimal place, so the product needs $1 + 1 = 2$ decimal places.
Placing the point gives $61.20$, so the product is $61.2$. This is close to the estimate $14 \times 4.5 = 63$.
